The appellant has filed this first criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 being aggrieved by order dated 13.01.2026 passed in Bail Application No.54 of 2026 passed by the Special Judge (Prevention of Atrocities),
Jabalpur District Jabalpur, MP whereby his regular bail application filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023, has been rejected.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant has pointed out that the appellant is innocent and has not committed any offence.

It is submitted that the statement of Chander Singh was recorded by the police NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26384 2 CRA-621-2026 after nine months' from the date of lodging of the FIR and it is only in the said statement that the role of the present appellant has been shown, that too on false and untenable grounds.
Even, Omprakash Tripathi, Ganga Pathak, Mrs. Mamta Pathak and other co-accused persons have not attributed any role of the present appellant in the alleged offence.

The allegation against the present appellant is that he arranged certain persons including arranging one Ram Kripal to impersonate Chander Singh and that by producing Ram Kripal as Chander Singh, the land was allegedly sold in favour of the purchasers.
However, except for the statement of Chander Singh, there is no material evidence available on record against the present appellant.
It is further submitted that although one more case of a similar nature has been registered against the appellant, he has been falsely implicated therein as well.

1 persons namely Ramkumar Manjhi and Narayan Prasad Shrivas, who were signatories to the sale deed have already been granted bail by this Court and the present appellant claims parity with them.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the investigation is complete and the charge-sheet has already been filed in the matter.
The appellant is in custody since 01.01.2026.
He is ready and willing to abide by any condition that may be imposed by this Court.
In the aforesaid circumstances, it is prayed that the appellant be enlarged on bail.

4 . Per contra, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail on the ground that Chander Singh in his statement has categorically stated that the present appellant arranged various persons, committed fraud and also facilitated impersonation by producing Ram Kripal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26384 3 CRA-621-2026 as Chander Singh.
It is submitted that although the name of the present appellant was not mentioned in the FIR, his entire role has surfaced during the course of investigation.

It is further submitted that, considering the role attributed to the appellant as reflected from the record and in view of the fact that another case of a similar nature has been registered against him, the acts alleged are grave in nature.
The offences are punishable with imprisonment for life; hence, the appellant is not entitled to be released on bail.
It is also submitted that the co-accused persons were signatories to the sale deed as witnesses.
Moreover, Narayan Prasad Shrivas was of advanced age (about 80 years), and thus, the case of the present appellant stands on a different footing.
The role attributed to the appellant is crucial in the commission of the offence, and therefore, he cannot claim parity with the other co-accused persons.
In view of the aforesaid, it is prayed that the appeal for bail be dismissed.
5. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the present appellant is not entitled to be released on bail.
It is contended that although respondent No.2 has been arrayed as a co-accused in the case, he is, in fact, in the position of a victim.
The sale proceeds were allegedly deposited in a fake account opened by the present appellant in the name of Chander Singh.
It is further submitted that the present appellant is the main accused in the commission of the offence.
In view of the aforesaid, it is prayed that the appellant be denied the benefit of bail.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
7.

In view of the rival submissions and upon perusal of the material NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:26384 4 CRA-621-2026 available on record, this Court finds that the role attributed to the present appellant is prima facie grave and material in nature, particularly in light of the statement of Chander Singh and the allegations regarding impersonation and fraudulent transactions and receiving the sale proceeds and the fact that another case of similar nature has also been registered against him.

Considering the seriousness of the allegations, the manner in which the offence is alleged to have been committed, the existence of a similar case against the appellant and the fact that there is no parity with the co-accused persons, who have been granted bail, this Court is not inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the appellant.
8. Accordingly, the appeal for grant of bail stands dismissed.
